taxonomies.desc: Student in an Organized Health Care Education/Training Program

patient_overview.name: Dominic Rivera
patient_overview.description: A 22-year-old Puerto Rican male college student recovering from a gunshot wound trauma. He is a community volunteer and feels protective over his younger siblings. He has a history of Type 2 Diabetes (prediabetic history) but is now poorly controlled. He is skeptical of healthcare systems and authority figures, showing resistance to standard medical advice. He has limited health literacy and low motivation to adhere to strict dietary or medication regimens. He values his role in the community and is protective of his family, which can be a lever for motivation but also a source of stress.

demographics.residence: Urban Latino neighborhood in Puerto Rico
demographics.language: Spanish (primary) and English (functional, but prefers Spanish)
demographics.cultural_context: Strong family ties, collectivist values, cultural foods include pork, rice, beans, plantains, coconut milk. Values 'cuidado' and respect for elders but struggles with 'authority' figures in healthcare. Trust issues stem from negative experiences during his trauma recovery.

medical_history: Recent emergency surgery for gunshot wound
current_symptoms: Mild headache and blurred vision occasionally
anthropometrics: Recent weight gain: 5 lbs over 3 months

medications.name: Metformin
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity and lower blood glucose
medications.patient_concerns: Experiences mild GI side effects; skeptical it will help; thinks diet alone can fix his sugar

supplements_and_otc: Coiflory root tea (as requested by his mother)

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Mediterranean-Latino, but high in refined carbs and processed meats
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Preference for sugary drinks (Jus de Piña)
Cooking frequency (often relies on pre-made foods due to trauma recovery)
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Irregular meals; often skips breakfast, eats lunch at work, dinners with family
nutrition_profile.hydration: High intake of sugary fruit juices and sodas; low water intake
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Low to moderate (walking for community work, no structured exercise)
nutrition_profile.sleep: Poor sleep quality due to stress and PTSD symptoms

psychosocial_profile.personality: Resilient and pragmatic, but skeptical of authority. He values independence and self-reliance, but feels frustrated by limitations imposed by his diagnosis and recovery. He is protective of his younger siblings and sees them as his motivation to be healthy, though he masks this vulnerability.
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Direct and occasionally blunt. He uses slang and may interrupt if he feels unheard. He prefers Spanish and may switch to English if the topic becomes clinical. He shows defensiveness when criticized but opens up when he feels respected.
goals: To regain independence and return to work
To lower his sugar levels so he can play with his siblings
concerns: Fear of losing his job as a volunteer
Concern about side effects of medication
Fear of becoming a burden to his family
beliefs: Sugar is not the only cause of diabetes
Healthcare professionals don't understand his culture
Diet is just about eating 'good' foods
motivations: Financial stability (wants to work and earn money)
strengths: Willingness to try if it feels practical
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Younger siblings and parents; neighbors who support him in community service
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Ambivalent; willing to try small changes but needs to see immediate benefits and feel trusted by his care team.

initial_information: He mentions feeling tired and thirsty often
He mentions eating rice and beans most of the time
He mentions his sister is sick
discoverable_information: He reveals he only takes his meds when he has a good day
He admits he likes juice over water
He mentions he works irregular hours
He shares he trusts his mother's advice more than doctors'
He mentions he skips breakfast to save money on lunch
reluctant_information: He initially hides that he skips breakfast to avoid cost
He hesitates to mention his trauma-related stress affects his eating
He hides his desire to be more active but feels too weak
He initially downplays the fear of being a burden to his family
hidden_information: He has a history of eating disorders related to body image and family dynamics
He is struggling with PTSD symptoms that affect his sleep and eating
He has been using supplements to lower blood sugar but knows they are not proven
He has a strong cultural belief that he should be the provider for his family
He is financially strained and cannot afford healthy food consistently

possible_patient_reactions: Defensiveness if the student starts diagnosing without listening
Reluctance to discuss food without being asked respectfully
Engagement when discussing family or community support
Skepticism if the PES is generic
Engagement if the PES addresses his specific barriers (e.g., food cost)
Disinterest if the strategy feels impractical
Openness to try new recipes if they are familiar
Resistance to 'Western' diet advice
Engagement when discussing family meals

opportunities.learning_objective: Integrate medication management with nutrition care
possible_patient_reactions: Defensiveness if reprimanded for non-adherence
Reluctance to discuss meds without permission
Engagement if the student addresses side effects empathetically
Resistance if the student is too directive
Engagement if the student uses open-ended questions
Skepticism if the student doesn't validate his experiences
Defensiveness if barriers are blamed on the patient
Engagement if the student offers practical solutions
Reluctance to discuss sensitive barriers (e.g., financial) without trust

expected_discoveries: Patient's need for mental health support
possible_patient_reactions: Skepticism of institutional resources
Engagement if the student involves family or community leaders
Openness to discuss mental health if framed as strength

assumptions: Patient has limited English proficiency but uses functional English
Patient's trauma history affects his mental health and sleep
Patient's family dynamics are supportive but not actively involved in his care
Patient's financial status is strained but stable enough to access care
optional_details: He has a pet dog that he cares for and walks
He attends a community meeting weekly to discuss local issues
He has a history of eating disorders related to body image
He has been using supplements to lower his blood sugar
He has a strong belief that he should be the provider for his family
